Subject:  Funding For Bluffs Park South Walkway Repair Project

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Provide a recommendation to the City Council to consider
appropriating $50,800 from the General Fund Undesignated Reserve for the repair of the
Bluff’s Park South Walkway for a total revised budget of $180,800.

FISCAL IMPACT: Funding for the Bluff’s Park South Walkway Project was included in the
Adopted Budget for FY 2023-24, for a total amount of $130,000. Based upon the
construction bids for this project, an additional appropriation of $50,800 from the General
Fund Undesignated Reserve to Account No. 310-9097-5100 (Malibu Bluff’s Park South
Walkway) is needed to perform these repairs. The projected General Fund Undesignated
Reserve at June 30, 2024, is $64,232,575.

  Existing Funding  Estimated Costs  Variance
GF Designated for CIP $130,000 Design Services  $27,900
  Construction  $132,900

WORK PLAN: This item is part of the day-to-day operations identified in the Adopted FY
2023-24 Strategic Priority Project List.

DISCUSSION: Council Policy #44 requires that all proposed appropriations over $10,000
be reviewed and discussed by the Administration and Finance Subcommittee prior to

  Page 1 of 2
  Agenda Item 3.A.
 being presented to the City Council. The proposed appropriation item will be presented to
the Council at its Regular meeting on January 22, 2024.

Over the past several years, staff have repaired or replaced several different sections of
the Bluff’s Park South Walkway, but it was determined a more in-depth repair was
required. In February 2023, Staff conducted a site visit to evaluate the existing condition
of the walkway and it was discovered the base of the walkway had experienced erosion
and had also been undermined by rodents. (Attachment 1). Staff discovered the natural
erosion of the grade and base, caused by our coastal nature, resulted in an approximate
1-foot drop off the walkway raising much concern over the safety of parkgoers.

This project consists of earthwork to build up the natural grade, the construction of a new
concrete deepened curb that will run alongside the walkway where erosion is most likely
to occur, and repair of damaged concrete panels. The project is intended to address
safety, erosion, and undermining of the walkway. The proposed deepened curb will only
be exposed approximately 4-inches and will act as a means to protect the base of the
walkway from erosion, as well as safeguard against rodents burrowing and undermining
the walkway. (Attachment 2).

On November 9, 2023, six contractors submitted construction bids for this project. The
lowest bid was $132,900 which, including the design costs and contingency, becomes
more than the approved budget for this project ($130,000). Additional appropriation is
needed to complete this project and repair the Bluff’s Park South Walkway. Staff
recommends that an additional $50,800 be allocated from the General Fund Undesignated
Reserve to execute a construction contract with the low bidder (Ardalan Construction
Company Inc.) and allow for potential change orders up to 15% of the contract.

Subject:  Funding for Skate Park Design and Civil Engineering Elements

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Provide a recommendation to the City Council on the
appropriation of $68,400 from the Designated Reserve for the Case/Crummer Parcel
for an Amendment to the Agreement with California Skateparks.

FISCAL IMPACT: An appropriation of $68,400 from the Designated Reserve for the
Case/Crummer Parcel to Account Number 310-9090-5100-00 (CIP – Skate Park) is
needed for the proposed amendment. The projected Designated Reserve for the
Case/Crummer Parcel on June 30, 2023, is $347,479.

STRATEGIC PRIORITY: This item supports the Permanent Skate Park priority
identified in the Adopted FY 2023-24 Strategic Priority Project List.

DISCUSSION: On February 24, 2020, the Council approved a Professional Services
Agreement (Agreement) with California Skateparks (Consultant) to provide design
services and construction documents for the Permanent Skate Park (Skate Park). The
Agreement included work related to the public design process, design engineering, and
construction documents.

On May 24, 2021, the Council approved Amendment No. 1 with the Consultant to
prepare architectural design plans for drainage, grading, erosion control, stormwater
control, landscaping, and project coordination and administration. The Civil Engineering
and Landscape Architect collaborating with the Consultant is RRM Design Group
(Subconsultant). The Subconsultant has successfully worked with City staff to prepare

  Page 1 of 2
  Agenda Item 3.B.
 design documents for the Coastal Development Permit, Environmental Review Board
(ERB), and Planning Commission Meetings.

The original landscape plan excluded an irrigation system and included a mixture of
hydroseed and native plants, requiring staff to hand water landscaped areas for over a
year until plant establishment. Following an analysis of the design, staff proposes
adding an irrigation system to the Skate Park landscape plan. Native landscaped areas
take up to a year to establish, and regularly scheduled irrigation would increase the
likelihood of successful plantings and less plant dieback. A consistent watering
schedule will ensure plants will be robust and aesthetically pleasing throughout the
year. Additionally, it would eliminate the need for maintenance staff to complete daily
to weekly hand watering. The City will use recycled water to irrigate native vegetation
and trees along the perimeter of the Skate Park and planters.

On August 15, 2023, the Parks and Recreation Commission approved a
recommendation to add a permanent restroom facility to the Skate Park. This amenity
will improve access to restrooms at the Skate Park and adjacent baseball fields. The
closest permanent restroom facility is located at the Michael Landon Center,
approximately 700 feet from the Skate Park. The Consultant will prepare Civil
Engineering and schematics for domestic and recycled water services.

Additional services provided by the Consultant and Subconsultant that were not
included in the original Scope of Work include the coordination and attendance at public
meetings such as ERB and Planning Commission.

Staff worked with the Consultant to prepare a proposal for the additional work
(Attachment). The proposed cost for the work is $53,800, which includes:

  • Design and construction management
  • Preparation of architecture design plans for City Council review
  • Irrigation plans and system layout, main line, automatic controller, piping, and
  locations of hydro zones for non-potable water sources
  • Landscape construction plans
  • Civil engineering for areas of the project not included in the Agreement
  • Project coordination and administration, where needed

The proposal also includes $14,600 in variable costs for landscape and skatepark
construction administration, which would be reduced if staff could assist in those areas.

If the Subcommittee recommends the appropriation of $68,400 from the Designated
Reserve for the Case/Crummer Parcel, the appropriation and an Amendment to the
Agreement with California Skateparks will be brought to Council in January 2024.

DESCRIPTION OF WORK TO BE PERFORMED
RRM Design Group, a California Corporation (“RRM Design Group”), has entered into an
agreement with California Skate Parks (the “Client”) with an effective date of May 24, 2021 (the
“Prime Agreement”) for the project: Malibu Skate Park Civil Engineering and Landscape
Architecture (the “Project”). Additional Services Authorized by the Client are subject to the
Terms and Conditions of the Prime Agreement.

In addition to the RRM Civil Engineering and Landscape Architecture services provided in the
Prime Agreement (dated July 12, 2021), RRM Design Group is proposing the following tasks to
develop a complete set of construction documents as required to obtain building permits for the
construction of the Malibu Bluffs Skate Park.

Landscape Construction Documents
The existing authorized Task C.2 includes the scope and fee for landscape construction
documents and specifications related to planting only. Excluded from the previous agreement
are the following supplemental documents needed for building permit issuance and final
approvals.

Irrigation Plans and Details
The irrigation plans will detail items such as irrigation system layout, main line, automatic
controller, head layout, piping, valve quantities, and locations indicating hydrozones for non-
potable water sources. In support of the irrigation plans, we will prepare irrigation details that
specify the method of construction and proper irrigation system component procedures. This
task includes water-use budgeting and calculations where needed to satisfy the requirements of
California’s Model Water Efficient Landscape Ordinance (MWELO) and the City of Malibu’s
development requirements.

Landscape Construction Plans and Details
Construction plans for the skate park layout with a keynoting system that identifies landscape
construction items and references to appropriate details. This plan will include and annotate site

Details for landscape construction items will be illustrated on the construction plans. The details

and flatwork design will be based on the project geotechnical report’s recommendations and
provided by RRM Civil Engineering in conjunction with California Skate Parks.

Irrigation and Landscape Construction Specifications
As a supplement to the current contract agreement, the landscape construction documents

provisions for irrigation and landscape construction items. This scope assumes that all general

construction documents.

MINUTES
  MALIBU ADMINISTRATION & FINANCE SUBCOMMITTEE
  SPECIAL MEETING
  DECEMBER 18, 2023
  TELECONFERENCED VARIOUS LOCATIONS
  -

  2:00 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to AB 361 and fully teleconferenced from various
locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Pro Tern Stewart called the meeting to order at 2:01 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance:

  PRESENT: Mayor Pro Tern Doug Stewart and Councilrnember Bruce Silverstein

  ALSO PRESENT: Joseph Toney, Assistant City Manager; Alexis Brown; Deputy City
  Manager; Renée Neerrnann, Finance Manager; Kristin Riesgo, Community Services
  Director, Brandie Ayala, Administrative Analyst, Parker Davis, Media Technician;
  Cynthia Alba, Executive Assistant; and Kathleen Stecko, Deputy City Clerk

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Councilmember Silverstein moved, and Mayor Pro Tern Stewart seconded a motion
  to approve the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried
  unanimously.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Deputy City Clerk Stecko reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted on
  posted on December 14, 2023.

ITEM 1  PRESENTATIONS

  None.

ITEM 2  OLD BUSINESS

  None.

ITEM 3  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Funding For Bluffs Park South Walkway Repair Project
  Recommended Action: Provide a recommendation to the City Council to consider
  appropriating $50,800 from the General Fund Undesignated Reserve for the repair
  of the Bluff’s Park South Walkway for a total revised budget of $180,800.
 Malibu Administration and Finance Subcommittee
Special Meeting
Minutes of December 18, 2023
Page 2 of 3

  Administrative Analyst Ayala presented the staff report and reviewed the details of
  the project request.

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart opened public comment, as there were no speakers in the
  meeting public comment was closed.

MOTION  Councilmember Silverstein moved, and Mayor Pro Tern Stewart seconded a motion
  to provide a recommendation to the City Council to consider appropriating $50,800
  from the General Fund Undesignated Reserve for the repair of the Bluff’s Park
  South Walkway for a total revised budget of $180,800.

  Mayor Pro Tern Stewart asked a question regarding the amount of the contingency.

  Administrative Analyst Ayala stated that staff hopes the contingency will not be
  needed and stated that they would like to be prepared to address concerns.

  Mayor Pro Tern Stewart inquired how long the stretch of construction is along the
  walkway.

  Administrative Analyst Ayala said that it was a 2500 square feet stretch, with a
  short construction timeline of about 30 days, depending on weather. She said the
  item would go to the City Council in January 2024.

  The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

  B.  Funding for Skate Park Design and Civil Engineering Elements
  Recommended Action: Provide a recommendation to the City Council on the
  appropriation of $68,400 from the Designated Reserve for the Case/Crummer
  Parcel for an Amendment to the Agreement with California Skateparks.

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented the agenda report, stating that the
  original project design did not include an irrigation system and this item also
  includes a design for a restroom facility.

MOTION  Councilmember Silverstein moved, and Mayor Pro Tern Stewart seconded a motion
  to recommend the City Council appropriate $68,400 from the Designated Reserve
  for the Case/Crummer Parcel for an Amendment to the Agreement with California
  Skateparks. The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

ADJOURNMENT

  At 2:11 p.m., Mayor Pro Tern Stewart adjourned the meeting.
